div.p: Multicore systems are rapidly immerging as a new paradigm for integrating both high performance systems and embedded applications. A large field of research focuses now on reconfigurable multicore architecture in order to find optimal solutions for improved performances such as energy consumption. A Perfect system would be able to create a balance between optimum resources allocation and a particular workload. The dynamic frequency scaling has been a key technique in exploiting the hardware configurable characteristics of processors. However, for large class of applications in embedded real time systems, the variable operating frequency interferes with their deadline guarantee. In this paper, a novel fuzzy logic technique is presented to optimize real time system feasibility and energy consumption in multicore architecture based on operating frequency scaling. Tested on different periodic task sets generated with different system charges the proposed technique is an intelligent decision aid system that studies schedulability and energy consumption aware.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: In recent year, there has been a rapid and wide spread of non traditional computing platforms, especially mobile and portable computing device. Embedded systems typically have to fulfill timing constraints that are related to their application domain and usage scenarios. Constraints are usually specified as the deadline to perform specific functions. Therefore, embedded designers must be able to evaluate which design alternatives can fulfill those constraints and guarantee real time behavior.

Simulation based techniques can be used to evaluate whether a particular MPSOC platform architecture is able to meet the timing constraints of an application. To guarantee the best hardware adaptation, this paper proposes a fuzzy logic reconfiguration technique to search a balance between power consumption and real time system schedulability. A fuzzy inference system (FIS) is a system that uses fuzzy set theory to map inputs into outputs. FIS uses a collection of fuzzy membership functions and rules, instead of Boolean logic, to reason about data. The functional operations in fuzzy expert system proceed in the following steps: Fuzzification, Fuzzy Inferencing (apply implication method), Aggregation of all outputs and Defuzzification.

The use of fuzzy logic to optimize the configuration of hardware architecture was adopted because it offers some advantages. First, detailed complex modeling of the system is not needed and human logic knowledge is captured. Second, it offers easily adaptative and light weight design support system. This paper describes the contribution of the approach in three main parts: The first paragraph is a state of art about dynamic frequency scaling in multiprocessing architecture and about fuzzy logic in embedded systems. The second part is dedicated to the proposed fuzzy technique architecture presentation. Finally, simulation and results are detailed.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: In real time embedded systems like portable medical devices and cellular phones, where tasks must be completed by some specified deadlines, most reconfiguration algorithms and techniques do not consider real time constraints and are based on solely average computational throughput [4].

div.head: A. Fuzzy Logic and Embedde Systems
div.p: An objective of fuzzy logic has been to make computers think like people, fuzzy logic can deal with vagueness intrinsic to human thinking and natural language [3]. Using fuzzy logic algorithms could enable machines to understand and respond to vague human concepts without having an exhaustive mathematical model. Almost every application, including embedded control applications, could reap some benefits from fuzzy logic. Its incorporation in embedded systems could lead to enhanced performance, increased simplicity and productivity.
The use of heuristic based methodologies to design space optimization for MPSoC involves the knowledge of processor characteristics in order to converge toward a final solution.

Qadri in [1][2] presented a fuzzy based reconfiguration for MPSoc that takes into consideration energy consumption and throughout of the real time system. This work argues the advantages of integration fuzzy inference system that calculates the number of cores and the operating frequency. In close loop architecture (fig ) the DSE is reconfigured until the system is stabilized.

div.head: B. Dynamic Frequency Scaling (DFS) in Multiprocessor
div.p: Architecture Significant research and developpement efforts have been made to study voltage and frequency scaling in MPSOC architecture. Many DFS algorithms are used to raise architecture performances. Typically, they use a simple feedback mechanism, such as detecting the amount of idle time on processors over a period of time and then adjust the frequency and voltage to just optimize computational load. The main idea of these studies is about avoiding wasting cycles by reducing the operating frequency which optimizes energy consumption. However, they cannot provide any timeliness guarantees and real time tasks may miss their deadlines. In fact, these algorithms are tightly-coupled with operating system's task management services, since the dynamic selection of DFS must be coupled to task computation time [4]. The main challenge is to guarantee that the deadlines will not be violated when frequency is reduced to decrease energy consumption.

The techniques outlined in this work assume the classic model of real time system in which a set of periodic tasks that are characterized with release time ri, period Ti, deadline Di and WCET (worst case computation time) Ci. As in classical treatments of the real-time scheduling problem [4], the relative deadline is assumed to be equal to period i.e a task must complete its execution before the next release of the task.

Given that the worst case computation time is supposed to be the time needed by the task to complete its charge in maximum operating frequency, a real time scheduler allocates processor time to the task in such way that it respects its deadline. In this section, we try to establish a relationship between operating frequency and system shedulability. A system is schedulable when all its tasks respect their deadline under designed architecture and specific real time scheduler. Many schedulability tests where associated with several schedulers. Being identified as optimal scheduling algorithm for this kind of real system, EDF is priority based scheduler.

For a set of n periodic tasks, when we assume that the platform is composed of m identical unit-capacity processors and that Usys is system utilization, system feasibility is assured if this sufficient and necessary condition (1) is satisfied [9]:
div.formula: Usys = C1/T1+ C2/T2 + C3/T3 + …… Cn/Tn ≤ m(1)

div.p: Assuming a specified frequency scaling factor α (0<α≤1) simple static DFS condition given by (1) becomes:
div.formula: Usys = C1/T1+ C2/T2 + C3/T3 + …… Cn/Tn ≤ m×α(3)
div.p: While applying these settings, observe that scaling the operating frequency by a factor effectively results in the worst case computation time needed by a task being scaled by a factor 1/α while the desired period and deadline remains unaffected. Many research papers treated this static frequency scaling in order to create a balance between feasibility test and architecture performance

div.head: III. RECONFIGURABELE FUZZY SYSTEM
div.p: The proposed algorithm is closed-loop architecture that tries to find a feasible solution of real time periodic model. Being enable to have a mathematical model that reflects all the information given bellow, fuzzy logic could be the solution that will control the design of DSE using linguistic terms.

div.head: A. System Model 1) Real time application model
div.p: In this paper, we assume a periodic task model. In this model, each task Γi=(ri1, Ci, Ti, Di) is characterized respectively by its first release time ri1, its computation time Ci, its period Ti and its deadline Di. Further, we focus our attention on implicit deadline task system (Ci<Ti=Di ). A task Γi invokes a series of jobs, each separated from its predecessor by Ti time units. We also assume that a single job of a task cannot be executed in parallel. We let n denote the total number of tasks in the system and Γn is a set of the n periodic independent tasks. The k th activation date of job Γi k is defined as ri k = ri1 + (k-1).Ti. This instance (job) of the task Γi must respect its relative deadline di k =ri k + Di .

div.head: 2) Configurable multiprocessor architecture
div.p: The proposed MPSoC is comprised of 16-core symmetric chip multiprocessor platform based on the Intel x86 architecture, employing a shared memory architecture. The platform incorporates L1 and L2 caches. The number of active cores and the processor frequency/voltage can be adjusted both for energy consumption optimization. Table 1. details MPSoC processors characteristics. The energy consumption and voltage/frequency information was obtained from Intel 486 GX embedded processor datasheet [7]. This particular architecture was chosen because our study is situated in homogenous and symmetric multicore architecture which will reduce the number of rules in fuzzy system.
The processor energy consumption per cycle is denoted Ed when we suppose that static energy is negligible. We suppose that our model doesn't need memory access or pipeline.
Energy consumption of the whole system will be calculated in multiplying Ed by the number of cores. Esys = (Ed1 + Ed2+……..+ Edm ) (4)

div.head: B. Fuzzy Architecture Reconfiguration
div.p: The main idea of the proposed architecture is to take advantage of fuzzy logic to avoid the establishment of a model describing the exact relations between input and output parameters. As shown in fig. 1, it's a classic feedback control system which is governed by the real time schedulability test. The system is stabilized when the system charge is around one. The fuzzy system involves: input and output variables identification, associating variables with appropriate membership functions, formulating rule base and defuzzification.

div.head: 1) Input and Output Varibles identification and fuzzification
div.p: The number of parameters were identified that can be modified dynamically in a reconfigurable MPSoC where they are considered as control variables of the close loop architecture. Input variables are: Un=Usys/m×α which is normalized system utilization that would reflect schedulability test and Esys which is normalized energy consumption. The fuzzy system output is the operating frequency. All cores will run through the same frequency. The number of cores is calculated in the feedback module.

Four linguistic variables were associated with the input and output variables. Which could be explained by the fact that the system have four scaling operating frequency. Trapezoidal membership functions were associated with each linguistic variable, as detailed in table II, III and IV.

div.head: 2) Rule base and Deffuzzification
div.p: To establish relationship between the input variables and output parameters, fuzzy logic rules were defined. There are standard criteria for the definition of the rule base. Some logic facts led us to the rule base detailed in table 5 which are:

When the system utilization Un is inferior to one then we could decrease the operating frequency trying to minimize energy consumption and the number of ideles. Working with lower frequencies must respect schedulabiliy test. When Un is superior to one the operating frequency is increased until it reaches one. If the system charge doesn't allow it the feedback module will augment the number of cores until stabilization. The output of the inference system is crisp value after defuzzification. Many defuzzification method are used such as centroid, mean and thresholds. In this work, Centroid (Center of gravity) method was adopted. The fact that the membership functions were centered on scaling values of normalized energy consumption and operating frequencies explains the fig. 2 variations. In fact, there are four stages for the operating frequency: When the system charge load is not important the operating frequency is at the minimum scaling value otherwise it rises from stage to another depending on energy consumption state.

div.head: 3) Implementation in python
div.p: The fuzzy logic engine was implemented using python 3.4 conforming to TCE 61131-7 standard [7]. The free Fuzzy logic module (Fuzzython) is an open source class library which is optimized for faster response. System total energy was calculated as the sum of each processor core energy supposing that the application tasks don't need cache. The whole application class diagram is illustrated with fig. 3. In order to perform the proposed architecture evaluation, a task generator was used to generate a set of periodic tasks within fixed total system load charge (random values with fixed sum). Task periods are generated with log-uniform distribution between 1 and 1000. The main emphasis of the proposed fuzzy reconfiguration technique is to assure balance between energy consumption and system schedulability. However, mainly it represents Decision Support System (DSS) for real time applications with periodic tasks feasability studies. The rule base was written while given schedulability test priority over energy consumption.

In order to fulfill our aims, the proposed algorithm starts the iteration 0 with initial parameters i.e number of cores (m=1), operating frequency (fi=fmax=33MHz), normalized energy consumption (1) and total system utlization Usys calculated from the task model.

It begins modifying the configurable parametrs and it completes the system configuration in two cases: the system utilisation is equal to one or it stays unvariant. The number of iterations needed to stabilise the system depends on real time application number of tasks and on system utilisation value. In fig 4 . (a) (b), we could notice that the final configuration on the most important set (Set 4 with 100 tasks) needed 17 iterations which prooved that it stabilises quickly. Both the system utilisation and the number of tasks affects proportionnaly the number of iterations. The impact of these iterations configuration on individual parametres is discussed as bellow:

Energy Consumption : It is abvious that fuzzy algorithm gives importance to system feasibility rather than optimizing energy consumption. Whith every value of m the fuzzy inference looks for the most appropriate operating frequency which influences directly the energy consumption. Fig 5 . Gives an abvious conclusion about the correlation of the mean energy consumption with the number of used cores in one hand and with the importance of system utilization.

Number of Cores : Initiated at 1, the number of required cores is directly affected with system utilization. When the operating frequency calculated by the fuzzy system is unvariant the application stills non schedulable the algorithm rises the number of cores. It could be noticed that when set of periodic tasks has important utilisation factor (Set 3 and Set 2) all cores are used with maximum operating frequency scaling. The system is then stabilized with (m=16 and fi=33 MHz). Our system is therefore not feasible under this architecture (see fig. 6). Fig. 6. Number of cores variation with total system load The decision support system is mainly responsible of system feasibility guarantee then it takes care of energy consumption. Let's take the case of Set 2 (n=30 and Usys=25.6): After 17 iterations, the system utilization with 16 cores and operating frequency equal to 33 MHz becomes 1.60. To maintain this result simulation scheduling within Global EDF, Global LLF, EDZL and Pfair algorithms on Set 2 were done conserving the Worst case computing time as the charge needed by each task.

In another hand, when considering task periodic Set number 1 with n=10 and Un=1.33, the fuzzy reconfiguration system is stabilized after 5 iterations: In this case the RT-application is schedulable with two processor m=2 and energy consumption is optimized when all processors are executed with fi=25MHz. The scheduling of the Set 1 tasks must be done with computing Time multiplied by 1/α=0.75 .

div.head: V. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper a novel reconfiguration fuzzy based algorithm for multicore architecture is presented. The proposed technique was used to find an overall balance between the feasibility of RT periodic application and energy consumption of the multicore architecture. A higher priority was attributed to system feasibility while writing the algorithm. It was developed using python and Fuzzython module. The simulation was executed in a multiprocessor run time developed that we develop on python.

The results discussed bellow showed the capability and usefulness of the detailed methodology especially when the system utilization doesn't exceed 27. Therefore, it can be concluded that the proposed reconfigurable fuzzy logic can produce an overall good performance where there is no need for exhaustive mathematical model. However, it will be interesting to study the effect of cache size and associativity on shedulability test.
